# Agent Architectures

Manipulation Action Models → Multi-Fingered Dexterous Hand Manipulation Research → Agent Architectures

Runtime architectures connecting high-level semantic/geometric planning or agents to reusable dexterous-hand execution backends. Record skill interfaces, planning and memory responsibilities, the actual low-level controller, and whether feedback triggers low-level phase switching or high-level replanning/recovery. | [AM.MAN.DEX.AGENT.2] <a id="am-man-dex-agent-2"></a> | **AdaClearGrasp｜Adaptive clearing · RL dexterous grasping · Failure replanning**<br>[AdaClearGrasp: Learning Adaptive Clearing for Zero-Shot Robust Dexterous Grasping in Densely Cluttered Environments](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.10616v1)<br>Zixuan Chen, Wenquan Zhang, Jing Fang, Ruiming Zeng, Zhixuan Xu, Yiwen Hou, Xinke Wang, Jieqi Shi, Jing Huo, Yang Gao<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `agent-architecture` `vlm` `task-planning` `adaptive-clearing` `cluttered-grasping` `skill-library` `model-context-protocol` [reinforcement-learning](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [ppo](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `geometry-aware-policy` `failure-recovery` `sim-to-real` `real-world` | AdaClearGrasp uses a VLM to choose direct grasping or push/pull clearing from the scene and execution feedback, invokes geometric planning skills and a PPO-trained GeoGrasp policy through MCP, and replans after failures to grasp targets in dense clutter.<br>**Evaluation scope:** The Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct planner emits tool calls and parameters; geometric planners execute clearing/reset skills, and failure reports change subsequent skill selection. GeoGrasp is a PPO-trained MLP with 59-D observations: normalized nearest-point vectors from 18 hand keypoints, target height, and TCP height/orientation. It outputs 19 joint increments (7 arm + 12 XHand) executed by PD control. Training uses Cube, Cup and Apple without clutter; evaluation covers unseen objects and real-robot transfer without fine-tuning. Hardware uses xArm7 + XHand; geometric observations require object meshes and FoundationPose pose estimates. Clutter-Bench contains 7 targets × 3 clutter levels × 10 layouts = 210 simulation scenes; hardware evaluation reports 18 scenes. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.10616v1) · [Project](https://chenzixuan99.github.io/adaclear-grasp.github.io/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.AGENT.4] <a id="am-man-dex-agent-4"></a> | **GOTT｜Cross-hand contact primitive · Object-trajectory interface · Staged execution**<br>[GOTT: Object-centric Dexterous Manipulation with a Reusable Cross-Embodiment Primitive](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.03861v2)<br>Yulin Liu, Lai Wei, Yen-Jen Wang, Akash Sharma, Pieter Abbeel, Henrik I. Christensen, Haozhi Qi<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `agent-architecture` `vlm` `affordance-reasoning` `future-aware-planning` `object-centric-control` `object-trajectory-interface` `reach-acquire-move` `skill-composition` `reusable-contact-primitive` `cross-embodiment` `cross-hand-transfer` `canonical-link-joint-representation` [reinforcement-learning](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [ppo](../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [contact-estimation](../../topics/tactile.md) `pose-feedback-tracking` `sim-to-real` `real-world` | GOTT interfaces through desired object trajectories and reach specifications: a VLM selects task-relevant contact regions, planning and IK select feasible approaches, a shared cross-hand PPO primitive establishes stable contact in closed loop, and a pose-feedback tracker executes the object motion, reusing contact skills across tasks, arms and hands.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Default VLM affordance selection and full-trajectory IK checks generate reaches; demonstrations/external models can also supply specifications. Acquire uses a PPO-trained MLP with local hand–object geometry and proprioceptive history to output wrist/finger deltas. A contact predictor triggers Move after sustained thumb-plus-finger contact; Move is geometric pose-feedback tracking, not RL. A 21-keypoint/26-joint-slot representation with masks shares weights without hand-specific codecs. Joint training uses XHand, Sharpa and Allegro. One checkpoint achieves 90%/90%/96% real grasp success on Franka–Sharpa/Franka–XHand/Tianji–XHand (50 trials each). Four Franka–Sharpa trajectory tasks achieve 80% overall success (10 trials each). Unseen-Allegro-variant zero-shot results are simulated. Planning and acquisition run sequentially; phase switching does not establish high-level feedback replanning. Tracking approximates a fixed hand–object transform and remains limited by occlusion and fine in-hand manipulation. | arXiv v2 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.03861v2) · [Project](https://dex-gott.github.io/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.AGENT.1] <a id="am-man-dex-agent-1"></a> | **RoboDexVLM｜VLM Agent · Task planning · Failure replanning**<br>[RoboDexVLM: Visual Language Model-Enabled Task Planning and Motion Control for Dexterous Robot Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2503.01616v1)<br>Haichao Liu, Sikai Guo, Pengfei Mai, Jiahang Cao, Haoang Li, Jun Ma<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `agent-architecture` `vlm` `task-planning` `skill-composition` `skill-library` `agent-memory` `open-vocabulary` `grasp-generation` `kinematic-retargeting` `failure-recovery` `real-world` | RoboDexVLM uses GPT-4o to compose predefined skills from language instructions, maps parallel-gripper grasp proposals to a dexterous hand through kinematics, and feeds execution failures, the current scene and history back to the VLM to replan skills for long-horizon manipulation and recovery.<br>**Evaluation scope:** GPT-4o receives instructions, scene observations, available skills and memory, and outputs calls and parameters over eight atomic skills. Grounding DINO + SAM localize objects; AnyGrasp proposals are calibrated to the hand, arm motions use kinematic trajectories, and fingers close to a force threshold. Depth changes and finger-position feedback check each skill; errors, images and history prompt replanning from the last successful skill, with at most three recovery attempts per task. Feedback changes skill plans and parameters; no new RL or end-to-end VLA action policy is introduced. UR5 + Inspire five-finger hand + D435i demonstrations include drawer retrieval, lid opening and fruit collection. The linked author repository is an extended implementation. | IROS 2025 / arXiv v1 / 2025 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2503.01616v1) · [Project](https://henryhcliu.github.io/robodexvlm/) · [Code](https://github.com/henryhcliu/robodex_vlm) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.AGENT.3] <a id="am-man-dex-agent-3"></a> | **DexGraspVLA｜Hierarchical VLA · Domain-invariant visual representations · Diffusion imitation learning**<br>[DexGraspVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Framework Towards General Dexterous Grasping](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.20900v5)<br>Yifan Zhong, Xuchuan Huang, Ruochong Li, Ceyao Zhang, Zhang Chen, Tianrui Guan, Fanlian Zeng, Ka Nam Lui, Yuyao Ye, Yitao Liang, Yaodong Yang, Yuanpei Chen<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `agent-architecture` [vla](../../topics/vla.md) `vlm` `task-planning` `visual-grounding` `object-mask-tracking` `domain-invariant-representation` `dinov2` `diffusion-policy` `imitation-learning` `action-chunking` `failure-recovery` `real-world` | DexGraspVLA uses a VLM to select successive grasp targets and bounding boxes, converts them into tracked masks with SAM/Cutie, and combines these with frozen DINOv2 features to guide a demonstration-trained diffusion arm-hand policy; the planner checks execution and selects the next target, while stable intermediate representations support generalization across objects, lighting and backgrounds.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Runtime target selection and outcome monitoring coordinate closed-loop execution. The controller uses imitation learning, not RL; feedback changes targets and action inputs, not weights. Successful grasps trigger scripted placing. Hardware: 7-DoF RealMan RM75-6F arm + 6-DoF PsiBot G0-R hand; 13-D joint targets, 64-step predictions with 6 steps executed before replanning in standard grasping. Training uses 2,094 successful demonstrations with 36 objects; 1,287 tests vary objects, lighting and backgrounds. Zero-shot means no fine-tuning for new scenes; the nonprehensile extension uses 1,029 additional demonstrations. | AAAI 2026 Oral / arXiv v5 / 2025 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.20900v5) · [Project](https://dexgraspvla.github.io/) · [Code](https://github.com/Psi-Robot/DexGraspVLA) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
